steps.title: Slide it up
steps.instruction: Move y = x² up by 3 so it lands on the dashed target y = x² + 3. Then press Check match.

steps.title: Slide it right
steps.instruction: Move y = x² two units to the right to match y = (x − 2)².

steps.title: Flip it
steps.instruction: Switch to y = |x| and reflect it in the x-axis to match y = −|x|.

steps.title: Squash it
steps.instruction: Switch to y = sin x and squash it sideways to match y = sin(2x).

steps.title: Put it all together
steps.instruction: Back to y = x². Match y = −(x + 1)² + 4: flip it, slide it left 1 and up 4.

up-1.text: Adding a number outside the function changes every y-value.

up-2.text: d moves the whole graph up or down.

up-3.text: Set d = 3, then press Check match.

right-1.text: Changes inside the bracket act on x.

right-2.text: y = f(x − c): a positive c moves the graph right. It feels backwards!

flip-2.text: Multiplying the whole function by −1 reflects it in the x-axis.

squash-1.text: Base graph first: choose sin x.

squash-2.text: b inside the function squashes the graph sideways by a factor 1/b, so the waves come twice as often when b = 2.

squash-3.text: Pick sin x, set b = 2, Check match.

combo-1.text: Do one transformation at a time: flip, then shift sideways, then shift up.

combo-2.text: −(x + 1)² + 4 means a = −1, c = −1 and d = 4. The vertex ends up at (−1, 4).

combo-3.text: Pick x², set a = −1, c = −1, d = 4, Check match.

observations.whatHappened: Changing d slid the graph up and down, changing a stretched it vertically and a negative a flipped it upside down. Changing c slid it sideways, but in the opposite direction to the sign you see in the bracket, and changing b squashed it sideways.
observations.why: In y = a·f(b(x − c)) + d, the numbers outside f (a and d) act on the y-values, so they do what you expect: multiply or add. The numbers inside act on x before f sees it. To get the same y-value as before at x − c = 0 you need x = c, so the graph moves right by c; and b(x) reaches each value 1/b of the way along, so the graph squashes by a factor of 1/b. That is why changes inside feel backwards.
observations.equationLatex: y = a,f ig(b(x - c) ig) + d
realWorld: Animators shifting and stretching motion curves
Audio equalisers and sound waves (stretching sin x changes the pitch)
Fitting a model curve to experimental data

prompts.question: How does the graph of y = f(x − 3) compare with y = f(x)?
prompts.explain: Inside the bracket feels backwards: x − 3 moves the graph 3 to the right.

prompts.question: Which equation reflects y = f(x) in the x-axis?
prompts.explain: Multiplying every y-value by −1 flips the graph over the x-axis. f(−x) reflects it in the y-axis instead.

prompts.question: y = sin(2x) compared with y = sin x is…
choices: squashed sideways by a factor of ½
stretched sideways by a factor of 2
prompts.explain: b = 2 inside the function makes the waves repeat twice as often: a horizontal stretch by factor ½.

captions.text: d is outside the function: it adds to every y-value, so the whole graph slides up.
c is inside the bracket. f(x − 2) slides the graph RIGHT by 2: inside changes feel backwards.
A negative a multiplies every y-value by −1: the graph flips over the x-axis.
b inside squashes sideways: sin(2x) fits two waves where sin x had one.
Combine them: flip with a, slide left with c = −1, lift with d = 4. The vertex lands at (−1, 4).
